  I couldn't hand this off to the `maintain-rails:gem-upgrade-planner` subagent because no agent-launch tool was available in this session, so I did the analysis myself. Two things break on Pagy 9.3.5: the app no longer boots until the `items` options are renamed to `limit`, and readers who request page 0 or an invalid page get an error instead of the first page. With the changes below, all tests pass on 9.3.5. The working repo was not modified.
  
  # Pagy 8.6.3 to 9.3.5 upgrade plan for Margin Notes
  
  ## Where the app uses Pagy
  - `/home/user/workspace/repo/Gemfile:32` pins `gem "pagy", "8.6.3"`.
  - `/home/user/workspace/repo/config/initializers/pagy.rb` loads the `items` and `overflow` extras and sets `:items` 10, `:items_param :per_page`, `:max_items` 50 and `:overflow :last_page`.
  - `/home/user/workspace/repo/app/controllers/notes_controller.rb:2,18` includes `Pagy::Backend` and calls `pagy(@notes)`.
  - `/home/user/workspace/repo/app/helpers/application_helper.rb:2` includes `Pagy::Frontend`.
  - `/home/user/workspace/repo/app/views/notes/index.html.erb:30,40,59-62` uses `@pagy.items`, `pagy_info(..., item_name:)`, `@pagy.pages`, `prev` and `next`, and `pagy_url_for(@pagy, page)`.
  - `config/locales/en.yml` has no Pagy keys. Pagy's JavaScript, CSS and nav helpers are not used.
  
  ## Required changes (all in one deploy, together with the version bump)
  
  **1. Rename `items` to `limit`.**
  - 9.3.5 has no `pagy/extras/items` file. The bump alone fails at boot with `LoadError: cannot load such file -- pagy/extras/items` (log: `/tmp/pagy-exp/logs/v9-bump-only.log`).
  - Change the initializer to `require "pagy/extras/limit"`, `Pagy::DEFAULT[:limit] = 10`, `[:limit_param] = :per_page` and `[:limit_max] = 50`.
  - In the view, change `@pagy.items` to `@pagy.limit`.
  - Keep the initializer's two explanatory comments; my experiment copy dropped them, but nothing requires that.
  - These renames do **not** work on 8.6.3: it has no `limit` extra and no `#limit` method. They cannot be done ahead of the bump.
  - Keep `:limit_param = :per_page` so existing bookmarked or shared URLs and the form field keep working. The upgrade itself changes no URLs.
  
  **2. Restore "invalid page shows the first page".**
  - 8.6.3's `pagy_get_page` treated anything below 1 as page 1 (`[params[:page].to_i, 1].max`).
  - 9.3.5 uses `(page || 1).to_i`, so `page=""`, `"0"`, `"-1"` and `"two"` all become 0. `Pagy.new` then raises `Pagy::VariableError: expected :page >= 1; got 0`.
  - The app has no `rescue_from`, so these requests return a 500.
  - The existing test `notes_controller_test.rb:74` catches this (log: `/tmp/pagy-exp/logs/v9-renamed.log`).
  - Fix: `pagy(@notes, page: [params[:page].to_i, 1].max)` in `NotesController#index`.
  - This fix also works on 8.6.3 (I ran the full suite on 8.6.3 with it applied). It can ship first as a separate preparatory commit.
  - Avoid overriding `pagy_get_page` instead: its signature differs between versions (`(vars)` versus `(vars, force_integer: true)`).
  
  ## Optional (not needed for the upgrade)
  - **Bad `per_page` values already fail on 8.6.3.** `per_page` set to `""`, `"0"`, `"-5"` or `"abc"` raises `VariableError` on both versions, so it is not a regression; only the message changes from `:items` to `:limit`. If you want it fixed, clamp the value or `rescue_from Pagy::VariableError` as a separate change, on either version.
  - **9.x's new keyset pagination and other extras.** Nothing here needs them.
  - **Pagy 10.** Its upstream rewrite is out of scope, but note there will be another API migration later.
  
  ## Mixed-version and rollback risks
  - Nothing Pagy-related is stored. There are no Pagy jobs, cached Pagy objects or database columns, and the test cache is `:null_store`.
  - The query string format is unchanged: `page` plus `per_page`. Links generated by either version work on the other, so old and new processes can run side by side safely.
  - Rollback means reverting the bump and the renames together. The page-clamping fix can stay because it works on 8.6.3.
  - If anything external (log alerts, Sentry grouping) matches the `VariableError` message, the text changes from `:items` to `:limit`. I didn't find any such matching in the repo, but external configs weren't checked.
  
  ## Checks I ran
  Everything ran in disposable copies `/tmp/pagy-exp/v8` and `/tmp/pagy-exp/v9`, with `.git`, `tmp` and `log` removed.
  - **Isolation:** each copy used its own database (`DATABASE_URL=postgres:///pagyexp_v8_test` or `pagyexp_v9_test`) with `RAILS_ENV=test` and `PARALLEL_WORKERS=1`. Active Storage wrote to each copy's own `tmp/storage`, the queue adapter was `:test`, and the cache was `:null_store`. The v9 copy installed gems into its own bundle path, `/tmp/pagy-exp/bundle`. I dropped both databases afterwards, and the repo's `git status` was still clean.
  - **Resolved dependencies:** the only lockfile change was `pagy (8.6.3)` to `pagy (9.3.5)`. Rails is 7.0.8.7 and Ruby is 3.3.6.
  
  | Variant | Command | Result | Log |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 8.6.3, unchanged | `bin/rails test` | 46 runs, 0 failures | `/tmp/pagy-exp/logs/v8-test.log` |
  | 9.3.5, bump only | `bin/rails db:prepare` / `bin/rails test` | LoadError for `pagy/extras/items` | `/tmp/pagy-exp/logs/v9-prepare.log`, `/tmp/pagy-exp/logs/v9-bump-only.log` |
  | 9.3.5 + renames | `bin/rails test` | 1 error (page `VariableError`) | `/tmp/pagy-exp/logs/v9-renamed.log` |
  | 9.3.5 + renames + page fix | `bin/rails test` | 46 runs, 325 assertions, 0 failures; `zeitwerk:check` OK | `/tmp/pagy-exp/logs/v9-fixed.log` |
  | 8.6.3 + page fix only | `bin/rails test` | 46 runs, 0 failures | `/tmp/pagy-exp/logs/v8-pagefix.log` |
  | Edge-case probe (temporary test) | `bin/rails test test/controllers/pagy_probe_test.rb` | Same results on both versions (bad `per_page` raises; `page=999` and `page=2abc` return 200) | `/tmp/pagy-exp/logs/v8-probe.log`, `/tmp/pagy-exp/logs/v9-probe.log` |
  
  The suite passing doesn't prove completeness. It covers the info text, `per_page` capped at 50, page overflow going to the last page, and prev/next links keeping the filters.
  
  **From reading the source, not run:** the 9.3.5 gem source I read is unpacked at `/tmp/pagy9/pagy-9.3.5`. `pagy_url_for` and `pagy_info(item_name:)` have the same signatures and output; `overflow: :last_page` behaves the same; the default limit is 20 but the app overrides it.
  
  ## Checks still to do
  - Run `bin/rails test:system` in the v9 copy; I did not run the browser suite.
  - Add a request test that `page=0` and `page=abc` return 200 with "Displaying notes 1-10". The existing test covers this, but it would also guard the preparatory commit on its own.
  - After deploying, watch for `Pagy::VariableError` and 500s on `/notes`.
  
  ## Open question
  - I didn't read the upstream CHANGELOG between 8.6.3 and 9.3.5 line by line. My conclusions come from diffing the code paths the app actually calls; any other renames wouldn't affect this app.
  
  ---
  
  **My notes**
  
  - **Not re-checked by me:** the commands, results and logs in the plan are the agent's own report. The logs are under `/tmp/pagy-exp/logs/` if you want to confirm them.
  - **Still unchecked:** the browser tests (`bin/rails test:system`) haven't been run on 9.3.5, and nobody has read the upstream changelog line by line for 8.6.3 to 9.3.5.
  - **Order to ship:** the page fix in `NotesController#index` works on both versions, so it can go out first on its own. The version bump and the `items` to `limit` renames have to go out together in one deploy.
